history.summary: The Shri Ashtavinayak Mandir at Shivnagar/Narayan Nagar, Latur, is a Ganesha temple built in South Indian architectural style with a rectangular main hall. The main chamber houses eight different idols of Lord Ganesha (the eight forms) and a 4-foot-tall marble Ganesha idol; the adjoining gardens with an artificial fountain hold a nearly 9-foot-tall statue of Lord Shiva. IDENTITY FLAG: this temple is NOT one of the canonical Ashtavinayak circuit of Maharashtra (the eight swayambhu shrines near Pune and Raigad) — it is a local Latur temple named for the eight forms of Ganesha. One travel page wrongly merges it with the canonical eight-temple circuit; disregard that claim. Listed address: Shivnagar/Narayan Nagar, Latur, Maharashtra 413512.

town_description: Latur is a major city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, known as an educational and trading hub with the distinctive circular Ganjgolai market at its centre. It lies about 2-3 hours south of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and is the administrative seat of Latur district.
